groups.notes: Nine eligible units, all integrated, all started at ladder index 0 - the only step this repository has ever measured. Recommendation retained unchanged. Group confidence is low despite n=9 because the sample is single-armed: costToAcceptance can rank units against each other but cannot rank steps against each other, which is what a start recommendation requires. Three of nine were accepted on the first review with no fix pass; six required at least one fix pass and re-review. That re-review rate is a hint that a stronger start might be cheaper, but the rubric's floor-raise grounds are not met: no capability failure was recorded on any unit, and no stronger step was ever run, so the required 25%-lower-median comparison cannot be computed. No floor lowering is possible either - index 0 is the lowest verified step - and for the same reason no boundary probe is schedulable below it. CONFOUND, stated explicitly rather than controlled: costToAcceptance here is driven jointly by attempt count and by context size, and the two are not separable in this telemetry. Issue #50 (large group) is the clearest illustration - accepted on the first review with zero findings and still the second most expensive unit in the run at $17.75 - and the same effect is present inside this group (#59 cost $24.32 across 3 attempts on a 1235-line single-file change, while #49 cost $7.30 across 3 attempts on a 187-line change). Any future ranking of steps by median costToAcceptance in this group must normalise for change size or it will attribute context cost to route quality. capabilityEscalation is recorded as 0 because the telemetry records no capability failure or route change on any attempt; it is not evidence that escalation was tried and unnecessary. Calibration 2026-08-05: no new telemetry for this group this run; only the externalReview refreshed.

Recommendation retained unchanged: four eligible units cannot carry a per-size threshold (raise needs >=2 capability failures OR >=2 cleanly-cheaper-stronger-steps with no regression; lower needs >=5 clean successes and lower-step median not higher than floor's). No floor change is schedulable. costRange and durationMsRange kept as-is: #109 ran on Claude/Codex subscriptions and surfaced no per-token cost or credits; the implementer wall-clock (~13 minutes) falls inside the existing [528s, 1614s] range so the bounds did not move. CONFOUND carries over from the previous calibration: costToAcceptance is jointly driven by attempt count and context size; the median ($13.09) is retained unchanged for the 4-unit aggregate but should not be compared across groups or against a future step's median without normalising for change size. The calibrationKeys vector was extended with three new keys observed on #109 ('deep-module-refactor', 'safety-ordering', 'cross-module-integration') so future planners matching a deep-module safety-ordering refactor land in this group; the prior pair-crud/lock-contention keys are retained. capabilityEscalation is 0 because the telemetry records no capability failure or route change on any attempt; it is not evidence that escalation was tried and unnecessary. implications: All measured costToAcceptance figures in this file were incurred at claude-sonnet-5 introductory pricing and are not directly comparable to observations recorded after 2026-09-01.

The +50% applies to the whole ladder bottom, so it narrows the price gap to claude-opus-5 without providing any evidence about its quality. It is a reason to re-run the comparison, not a reason to change the floor.

claude-fable-5's $10/$50 pricing is 5x the sonnet-5 introductory rate and 2x opus-5; without measured capability evidence in this repository it cannot be promoted into the ladder on price alone, and the user directive excluding it from the ladder is unchanged.
